subject: SLA attribution for customer-network incidents — request for appendix
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@heliomed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@heliomed.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: SLA question: private VPC / peering outages and attribution

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our infra team asked a practical question about the Private/VPC contract language: how will Redwood attribute incidents that are caused by our customer-controlled network (on-prem peering, cross-connects, or our managed firewall)?

Specifically: if our users see latency or failed inference because our peering router flaps or an MPLS hop increases RTT, will HelioMed be automatically excluded from any SLA (credits or uptime guarantees) or do you have an "attenuation" or apportioned-credit approach? Procurement wants the exact wording that would go into the SOW or appendix so they can pass it to legal.

We'd also like to understand the kinds of evidence Redwood would accept for attribution (packet captures, BGP flaps, cloud peering logs) and any monitoring endpoints we need to expose. Can you share a proposed appendix and a short list of required telemetry?

Thanks — Samantha

Samantha Cho
Head of Cloud Ops, HelioMed

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@heliomed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA question: private VPC / peering outages and attribution

Hi Samantha — great question and an important one to get into the SOW.

Short answer: for Private deployments we do not automatically blanket-exclude incidents where the customer network is a contributing factor. Instead, we propose an "attribution appendix" that defines (1) a process for evidence submission, (2) an attribution window, and (3) an attenuation model for credits where the root cause is outside Redwood control but the customer network contributed to the outage/latency.

I'll attach a first-draft appendix that captures our recommended language and the telemetry we typically accept (BGP state change logs, peering router syslogs, cloud VPC flow logs, and pcap snippets). Key points up front:
- Redwood maintains uptime/latency SLOs on the service fabric under Redwood control.
- Customer-managed network faults that are demonstrated by accepted evidence will be excluded from Redwood's uptime credit calculations, but we will not remove latency SLOs entirely; instead we apply a proportional attenuation factor tied to the fraction of time the service was demonstrably outside our control.

Looping in Karthik and Laura to confirm legal and product wording. If this approach works for HelioMed we'll schedule a short call to walk through the appendix and the kinds of logs you should prepare.

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft-apdx.pdf (SLA appendix draft, redlined)

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA question: private VPC / peering outages and attribution

Irene / team — +1 to the approach. A few legal/product considerations to bake into the appendix:

1) Evidence standard: require "good-faith, time-correlated" telemetry showing a clear network path failure or sustained RTT deterioration (>=3x baseline for >5m) originating in the customer-managed segment. Acceptable artifacts: pcap excerpt with timestamps, BGP NOTIFICATION/state-change time series, cloud VPC flow logs, or third-party monitoring alerts (e.g., ThousandEyes trace).

2) Attribution window: we propose a default 2-hour window around the incident for evaluation; the appendix should allow Redwood to consider up to 24 hours for complex routing convergence cases.

3) Attenuation model: rather than an automatic exclusion for all SLA calculations, apply a proportional adjustment. Example: if total service downtime for an incident is 60m and the customer network is shown to have been impacting performance for 40m, only the 20m would be counted against Redwood uptime, and any credit calculations would be scaled accordingly.

4) Monitoring endpoints and rights: the customer must provide one or more monitoring endpoints or an agreed log export (S3/GCS) for the period under review; we should include a minimal list of required fields for logs.

5) Non-repudiation: signatures from the customer's networking lead should be acceptable; for contested cases we keep an engineering review panel (Redwood + customer) to adjudicate.

I'll add suggested clause text to the draft. Small ask: product to confirm whether latency SLOs should have a separate attenuation threshold vs availability SLOs.

—Karthik

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@heliomed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed appendix and next steps

Samantha — attaching the draft appendix per our earlier note. The draft includes:
- A short definition section (what counts as "customer-managed network"),
- Evidence types we accept,
- Attribution window & evaluation timeline,
- An attenuation formula and example calculation, and
- Operational steps for escalation and adjudication.

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft-apdx.pdf
Also included: network-trace-sample.txt (pcap excerpt converted to text) so your team can see the type of artifact we reference.

Would you be able to review and flag any required procurement/legal redlines? If it helps, I'm available for a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT.

Best,
Irene

From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@heliomed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_cho@redwood.com>
Cc: HelioMed Procurement <procurement@heliomed.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@heliomed.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed appendix and next steps

Thanks Irene — we've reviewed the draft and the proposal is promising. Procurement has two asks before we can proceed to signature: (1) an explicit responsibilities table (Redwood vs HelioMed) in the appendix, and (2) an itemized list of the telemetry fields Redwood requires (timestamp, src/dst IP, ASN, BGP state, RTT sample, tcp retransmits) with example retention locations.

We can do the 10am PT call tomorrow — Rajiv and our networking lead will join. After the call, procurement will provide a one-page redline and then we can route the finalized appendix to DocuSign.

Also: confirm that the attenuation math will be applied to both availability credits and latency SLA calculations.

Samantha

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

They confirmed they can provide pcap excerpts and BGP logs to an S3 bucket we specify. Procurement also wants the attenuation math explicitly called out for both availability and latency credits — product accepted that.

Action items for us:

- Karthik: review the final legal language for the responsibilities table and signoff on adjudication process.
- Tessa: prepare a DocuSign envelope template with the appendix attached (deal HM-4721).

I'll send the redlined appendix back to HelioMed when we have those edits. Good to proceed.

Irene

Redwood Inference
